kg_child_context_reason: KG child context is not useful because sd_data_master has no child modules in DEPENDENCY_CONTEXT and the generated fragments do not instantiate or wire submodules; they only drive external control/status interfaces.
code_gap_notes: The module interface is only a commented skeleton, so exact port directions and widths are needed for a legal merge.
Generated fragments procedurally assign several outputs in both the sequential block and the combinational output block, so merge must resolve output ownership to avoid multiple drivers.
bd_cnt is declared conditionally in the parameter fragment rather than with the other registers, and its reset expression depends on READ_CYCLE rather than an explicit width.
The RAM width conditional uses RAM_MEM_WIDTH_32/RAM_MEM_WIDTH_16, while the global defines context only shows RAM_MEM_WIDTH as 32, so external define handling must be reconciled.
Command, BD-fetch, FIFO-start, transfer-complete, CRC, retry, and Dat_Int_Status behavior are spread across fragments and need the detailed FSM output rules for consistent merge.
selection_reason: S004 is required as the current module input interface block, defining input port names, widths, and meanings.
S005 is required as the current module output interface block, defining output port names, widths, and status/control ownership.
S007 is needed to validate internal register declarations, widths, and which interface outputs are registered values.
S008 is needed for command constants, FSM one-hot state encodings, retry maximum, READ_CYCLE, and BD_EMPTY parameters used directly in the fragments.
S009 is needed for external define-dependent behavior, especially RAM_MEM_WIDTH, BD_WIDTH, BD_SIZE, READ_CYCLE, BD_EMPTY, and bd_cnt width.
S011 is needed to verify and merge the combinational next-state logic present in the generated fragments.
S014 is needed for the FSM sequential clock/reset behavior and active-high asynchronous reset requirements.
S015 is needed for per-state output/register update behavior, including BD loading, command handshakes, FIFO starts, transfer completion, stop command, retries, and Dat_Int_Status reset.
